findings.title: Rendering a small table can allocate gigabytes from an unchecked span
findings.summary: Rendering an admitted DOCX trusts `gridSpan`, `gridBefore` and `gridAfter` as allocation dimensions. A span of 1073741824 requests a 4 GiB column vector; embedded HTML `colspan` independently generates that many XML columns.

severity.rationale: High-likelihood deterministic denial of service at an untrusted document/library boundary; impact is host availability, with remote deployment and blast radius unspecified.

confidence.rationale: Parent independently traced actual current source, checked relevant controls and sibling operations; no application code or exploit input was executed.

codeEvidence.explanation: Summed spans directly determine f32 vector length.

codeEvidence.explanation: An embedded chunk supplies a positive usize colspan.

codeEvidence.explanation: The requested logical width sets loop iterations and generated XML size.

rootCause.summary: `cell_span()` and `row_grid_skip()` parse positive document-controlled integers without a logical-column cap. `table_block()` sums those spans into `occupancy` and passes it to vector allocation. The HTML importer repeats the same missing column-bound control before generating one `gridCol` per column.

findings.remediation: Apply a supported logical-column cap to DOCX and HTML spans and row skip counts, checked-sum row occupancy, and refuse over-budget tables before allocation or XML generation.

findings.title: An EOCD marker in a ZIP comment bypasses the archive entry budget
findings.summary: Package preflight reads the count from the last raw EOCD marker, while the ZIP reader skips invalid candidates. A fake zero-count end record in the real ZIP comment lets an archive exceeding `max_entries` be indexed and processed.

severity.rationale: High-likelihood deterministic denial of service at an untrusted document/library boundary; impact is host availability, with remote deployment and blast radius unspecified.

codeEvidence.explanation: The actual count is only compared in the duplicate-loss direction.

codeEvidence.explanation: PartFs trusts the same preflight then opens/processes the consumer-selected archive.

rootCause.summary: `declared_entry_count()` trusts a signature and two count bytes without validating the record's central-directory offset. zip 9.0.5 rejects an impossible zero-count offset and resumes its backward search to the real EOCD. `admit()` only checks for fewer indexed entries than declared, while `read_package()` has no actual entry-count recheck.

findings.remediation: Make preflight select and validate the same EOCD/ZIP64 structure the consumer uses before allocating its index, and additionally enforce the actual indexed entry count. Do not trust the final signature alone.

Installed zip9.0.5 find_central_directory.rs149-156 rejects zero-file offsets beyond the EOCD and continues; zip_archive.rs178-235 retries candidate metadata failures.
limitations: No runtime reproduction; deployment isolation and externally imposed quotas were not supplied.

findings.title: Nested legacy DOC field results cause quadratic character processing
findings.summary: A legacy DOC can nest many field result regions. For every character the reader scans all active field states; when they are all in result mode the short-circuit never fires, producing quadratic CPU work.

severity.rationale: High-likelihood deterministic denial of service at an untrusted document/library boundary; impact is host availability, with remote deployment and blast radius unspecified.

codeEvidence.explanation: Story processing is called on the decoded main text.

codeEvidence.explanation: An ordinary legacy convert operation reaches the field processor.

codeEvidence.label: Legacy hint caller
codeEvidence.explanation: A generic document refusal also executes this parser for a conversion hint.

rootCause.summary: `Story::blocks()` keeps a bool stack, computes `fields.iter().any()` for every character, pushes true on field begin, and sets the top false on separator. Repeating begin/separator pairs makes an ever-growing all-false stack; closing fields later keeps the input paired but does not undo the prior quadratic cost.

findings.remediation: Track the count of active code states alongside the stack so in_code is O(1), and enforce a field nesting limit.

findings.title: Shallow XML with unquoted attributes bypasses admission depth and exhausts the DOM stack
findings.summary: Package admission accepts shallow XML with HTML-style unquoted attributes. The recursive DOM parser treats the first value character as a quote delimiter, swallowing closing tags and nesting following siblings; an admitted depth-two pattern can therefore exhaust the host stack.

severity.rationale: High-likelihood deterministic denial of service at an untrusted document/library boundary; impact is host availability, with remote deployment and blast radius unspecified.

confidence.rationale: Parent independently traced actual current source, checked relevant controls and sibling operations; no application code or exploit input was executed.

codeEvidence.explanation: The DOM interprets x as a quote and consumes document structure until the second x.

codeEvidence.label: Recursive element descent
codeEvidence.explanation: The changed interpretation makes following siblings recursive descendants without a depth guard.

rootCause.summary: `check_xml_depth()` uses `TagPolicy::tolerant()` with quick-xml's `html_attributes()`, accepting `b=x`. `parse_element()` unconditionally takes the next character as a quote and scans to the next matching character. In `x>` it consumes the closing tag as attribute content, then recursively treats the following sibling as a child, without its own depth bound.

findings.remediation: Make accepted attribute grammars consistent, preferably refusing unquoted attributes at untrusted package boundaries, and enforce actual DOM recursion depth independently before recursive descent.

Attribute widths and XML byte sizes remain small; no giant archive or raised depth limit is required.
limitations: No runtime reproduction; deployment isolation and externally imposed quotas were not supplied.

findings.title: Recording a Node CLI plan follows a predictable temporary symlink
findings.summary: When recording operation flags into a plan, the Node CLI writes a predictable PID-named partial file without exclusive creation. A distinct local attacker who can create names in the plan directory can redirect that write to another victim-writable file.

severity.rationale: Potentially high-impact file corruption requires a local directory writer, PID/name prediction, and victim authority beyond that attacker; constrained low-likelihood path is low.

confidence.rationale: Parent independently traced actual current source, checked relevant controls and sibling operations; no application code or exploit input was executed.

codeEvidence.label: Plan recording dispatch
codeEvidence.explanation: Operation flags with --plan enter recordPlan rather than a normal edit.

codeEvidence.label: Predictable temporary write
codeEvidence.explanation: A local directory writer can precreate the PID-named partial as a symlink before the truncating write.

codeEvidence.label: Native secure sibling
codeEvidence.explanation: Rust now uses publication instead of opening its legacy partial name; do not generalize the Node defect to native.

rootCause.summary: `recordPlan()` derives `.<target basename>.<pid>.partial` beside the plan and passes it to `fs.writeFileSync()` with default truncating/follow-symlink semantics. Rename happens only after the redirected write; no private staging, exclusive-create or no-follow control protects this temporary name.

findings.remediation: Use exclusive creation in a private unpredictable staging directory beside the destination, verify/write the opened handle, then atomically publish; fail if any staging name already exists.

counterEvidence: Ambient output paths intentionally selected by the operator are not themselves vulnerabilities; the attacker controls an auxiliary temporary entry instead.
The native Rust recorder no longer opens its legacy predictable partial path and uses secure publication; this finding is Node-only.
Private directories without another writer prevent the attack. dry_run avoids the write.
limitations: No runtime reproduction; deployment isolation and externally imposed quotas were not supplied.

findings.title: Opening repeated relationships performs quadratic duplicate-repair scans
findings.summary: A shallow `.rels` part containing many distinct relationship IDs each duplicated identically passes supported repair rules. For every duplicate, the package reader linearly searches a growing vector of repaired IDs, causing quadratic CPU use inside normal package opening.

severity.rationale: High-likelihood deterministic denial of service at an untrusted document/library boundary; impact is host availability, with remote deployment and blast radius unspecified.

confidence.rationale: Parent independently traced actual current source, checked relevant controls and sibling operations; no application code or exploit input was executed.

codeEvidence.label: Relationship record collection
codeEvidence.explanation: Each XML record is parsed and appended, so identical duplicate records reach repair.

codeEvidence.label: Linear repaired-ID membership
codeEvidence.explanation: Every new duplicated ID searches all prior repaired IDs.

codeEvidence.label: Package-open consumer
codeEvidence.explanation: Both package and part relationship sets are repaired on normal opens.

rootCause.summary: `read_relationships()` preserves raw records in `items`. `drop_repeated_relationships()` uses a hashmap for the first-seen record but `Vec::contains()` to deduplicate the repaired-ID output. With N ID pairs, successful duplicate handling performs about N(N-1)/2 string comparisons. `PartFs::open_within()` always invokes the helper on package and part relationships.

findings.remediation: Use a HashSet for repaired-ID membership while preserving a separate ordered Vec for output, or add each ID once based on a bounded seen-state transition. Consider an explicit relationship-record budget.

counterEvidence: Conflicting duplicate IDs are rejected promptly; the attack uses exactly identical pairs the code intentionally repairs.
Attribute count caps constrain each tag, not the number of sibling relationship records.
HashMap seen prevents one quadratic lookup but does not bound the repaired Vec membership scan.
limitations: No runtime reproduction; deployment isolation and externally imposed quotas were not supplied.
validation.summary: Attacker .rels XML with N distinct identical ID pairs -> metadata_records/from_xml per record -> items includes duplicates -> drop_repeated_relationships -> repaired.contains scans growing vector.

controls: Conflicting duplicate IDs are rejected promptly; the attack uses exactly identical pairs the code intentionally repairs.
